_note: Set B, VERSIONED WITH THE RULES (11 files: top p1..p8, bottom p1..p3). tableVersion 1195-1 — the bytes are IDENTICAL to 1114-1: the setup-boundary gate (a one-setup job no longer merges same-diameter siblings) restores the ⌀3.175 × 12 metal O-flute primary, the ⌀3.175 ball × 10 finish, the ⌀2 × 12 rest and the ⌀1.5 × 6 curved rough, and the freeing contour stays on the ⌀3.175 × 42 whose STATED 42 mm flute proves the 25.3 mm profile (#1195). The priced pick then lands on the same cutters the 2026-11-09 bench used, byte for byte. The e2e reads this table as the cross-door check.
rule: (a) A CANDIDATE CHAIN IS RANKED BY THE TIME IT WILL REALLY TAKE (#1186 rule 1), ties to fewer bit changes then owned; (b) EVERY FLAT MAY PROPOSE AS A PRIMARY, shortlisted to the incumbent and the best own-row flat (#1192), and a cutter that can FREE the profile always joins when none shortlisted can (#1195); (c) THE FREEING CONTOUR IS A HARD CONSTRAINT (#1195, the analyst’s field): no chain is a candidate without a cutter whose STATED flute reaches the profile’s actual posted depth; the pick refuses only when nothing owned reaches or the operator pinned a cutter that does not, with a named sentence; (d) ONE CUTTER PER SHAPE AND DIAMETER, only on a job with a setup boundary (#1186 rule 6, gated by the setup count).
source: casemaker cut <job>.cutjob.json --location ~/setb-inputs/location.json --catalogue ~/setb-inputs/catalogue.json, branch 1195-freeing-reach @ 9338152b2 (1186-bench + the setup-boundary gate + #1195), k3, 2026-11-10; the CLI output is byte-identical to tableVersion 1114-1
